Source_Name: IMO Resolution MEPC.364(79) (CO2); EU Regulation 2015/757 Annex I/II as amended by 2023/957
Source_URL: FuelEU Maritime Annex II (CH4 slip default); ICCT 'Options for Reducing Methane Emissions from New and Existing LNG-Fueled Ships' (Oct 2023)
column9: CO2_TtW (2.750) is combustion-only and assumes zero slip - the true figure depends entirely on engine technology, which this fleet-wide file cannot know per-vessel (LNG is priced in this app but never burned - see src/lib/types.ts). CO2e uses CO2e = (1-slip)x2.750 + slipx28 (GWP100 AR5 CH4=28). CO2e_TtW_MT_Per_MT (3.533) is the EU MRV/FuelEU Annex II regulatory default: 3.1% w/w slip, 4-stroke low-pressure Otto-cycle dual-fuel (the most common retrofit/newbuild engine type). Full documented range: ~2.80 t/t at 0.2% slip (2-stroke high-pressure diesel-cycle, e.g. ME-GI - the cleanest option) up to ~3.71 t/t at 3.8% slip (measured worst case, per ICCT). Above ~1.3% slip, LNG's CO2e EXCEEDS VLSFO's combustion-only CO2 (3.114) - the well-documented finding that methane slip can erase LNG's on-paper CO2 advantage. Same regulatory framework (Annex I/II factors x GWP) underlies both EU MRV reporting and EU ETS surcharge liability for shipping (CO2 phased in from 2024, CH4+N2O from 2026) - one figure set serves both, nothing EU-ETS-specific to add.

Notes: Matches CH3OH stoichiometry to 3 s.f.: 1 carbon per 32.04 g/mol molecule, so Cf = 44.01/32.04 = 1.373 - within rounding of IMO's published 1.375, a useful cross-check that the source figure is transcribed correctly. CO2e adds the same +0.049 t/t CH4+N2O uplift as the conventional liquid grades (no significant slip mechanism for a liquid distillate-like fuel; small N2O contribution assumed similar in kind). MEOH_VLSFOe and MEOH_MGOe (src/lib pricing) are the same physical methanol restated as energy-equivalent prices, not separate fuels - they share this row.

column9: C19H36O2 (methyl oleate, a representative FAME ester): carbon fraction 228.2/296.5 = 0.770 by mass; CO2_TtW = 0.770 x (44.01/12.011) = 0.770 x 3.664 = 2.82 t CO2/t. Cross-checked against EPA's Table 1 stationary-combustion Biodiesel(100%) factor (73.9 kg CO2e/MMBtu), converted via EPA's default B100 heat content (0.128 MMBtu/gal) and density (~3.33 kg/gal): 73.9 x 0.128 / 3.33 = 2.84 t/t - the two independent methods agree within 1%, giving reasonable confidence despite no single primary source stating a marine-FAME Cf directly (IMO's Cf table has no biodiesel line; MEPC.1/Circ.905's biofuel Cf is a well-to-wake lifecycle figure for CII policy, deliberately not used here per the tank-to-wake basis this file follows). 100% FAME baseline used only to derive the B24/B40 blend figures above - not itself a Grade code in src/lib/types.ts. CO2e adds the same +0.049 t/t uplift.
